messages:
infra-bot: Alert triggered: HIGH_LATENCY_STREAMING on hosted/stream-generate — threshold breach at 03:12 UTC. severity: page. paging oncall. incident id: INC-20260315-82

karen: I got the page. jumping in. initial read: p99 latency spike, several streaming sessions dropped with 504s. no embedding impact.

josh: grabbing logs. can someone confirm whether this coincides with the 03:05 deploy?

priya: i see a config change event at 03:06: `deploy/routing-v5` rolled to canary pools. also a KV cache rollout at 02:58 (kv_ttl=8s -> 5s). both visible in deploy stream.

karen: thanks. primary hypothesis: aggressive TTL + routing weight change caused increased cache churn and reroutes to quantized backends.

pager-bot: Auto-escalation: paging secondary in 10m if unresolved.

luke: i'll start by disabling routing-v5 on canary. command: `infra rollback routing-v5 --target=canary --reason=\"INC-20260315-82\"`

josh: while luke does that, i'm going to mute noisy pages for the next 45m for the rules:`streaming_timeout.rate > 0.5%` and `p99_latency > 2s` (non-critical for dev accounts). will leave enterprise page thresholds intact.

priya: snippet for muting (audit):
```
POST /alerting/api/mutes
{ \"rule\": \"streaming_timeout.rate\", \"duration\": \"45m\", \"owner\": \"josh\", \"note\": \"mute during INC-20260315-82 mitigation\" }
```

luke: rollback finished. observing canary traffic rebalancing. error_count dropping in canary.

karen: good. i want us to be conservative: do not rollback global kv_ttl yet. instead: revert kv_ttl on canary only to 8s. lmk when done.

josh: applying targeted config: `configctl set kv_ttl=8s --scope=canary --change-id=rollout-441`

infra-bot: change accepted. rollout-441 started.

luke: metrics: canary p99 down from 3.2s -> 0.9s in 6m. prod stable for now.

karen: customer impact check: support queue shows 14 streaming tickets in last 30m, mostly low-tier. enterprise accounts: 0. estimated affected sessions: ~1.7% of active streams.

priya: ok, post-incident action item: alert tuning. current behavior pages on any p99 > 1.5s. that's noisy for ephemeral canary regressions. propose new policy: page if p99 > 1.5s AND error_rate > 1% OR affected_sessions_pct > 3%. otherwise create ticket to oncall channel.

josh: +1. also propose automatic 20m suppression of pages for config-rollout events unless the error thresholds are met. Reduce wakeups for planned changes.

karen: also add: route config-deploy events to #eng-deploys and create a low-priority digest in #eng-oncall. page only if post-deploy threshold breaches occur.

luke: to be concrete i'll draft a rule patch. snippet idea:
```yaml
- alert: StreamingLatencyConfigImpact
  expr: |
    (increase(config_change_events_total{kind="routing"}[10m]) > 0)
    and (
      (p99_stream_latency > 1.5 and error_rate > 0.01)
      or (affected_sessions_pct > 0.03)
    )
  for: 5m
  severity: page
  annotations:
    runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/streaming-latency
```

priya: also please add a dashboard panel `canary/config-impact` that overlays config events on top of p99 and kv_cache_miss rate. it's valuable for post-deploy triage.

josh: i'm going to open a PR with the alert changes and include unit tests (simulate metrics and config event spikes). i'll tag infra and oncall for review.

karen: follow-ups and owners:
- josh: PR for alert routing + suppression (2h)
- priya: create dashboard and link in runbook (4h)
- luke: produce timeline and attach diffs for routing-v5 vs v4 (1h)
- karen: draft incident summary + customer impact notice (30m)

pager-bot: Handoff reminder: oncall shift change in 45m.

karen: thanks team. mitigation successful, we'll keep canary ttl at 8s until we validate further. once josh's PR merges we'll roll the alert routing policy so config changes don't page by default. i'll create the postmortem doc and link the graphs.

josh: PR up in 10m. tagging @infra @eng-oncall. includes changelog entry and tests.

luke: leaving monitoring watch for 2h. will escalate if instability recurs.

infra-bot: Incident INC-20260315-82 status -> mitigated. severity -> P2.

karen: handoff to luke in 40m. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
